primary_work.title: Learning Unknown Intervention Targets in Structural Causal Models from Heterogeneous Data

decision: NARROWED BEYOND HETEROGENEOUS-DATA UNKNOWN-TARGET IDENTIFICATION — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: changing exogenous noises can be recovered from heterogeneous environments without language under stated assumptions
unknown soft-intervention targets are uniquely identifiable under causal sufficiency and T-faithfulness
latent confounding permits only a graphically characterized candidate superset
language-assisted candidate-set reduction does not imply joint semantic identification
counterexample: Under latent confounding, two SCMs can share every environment-indexed observed distribution, recovered changing-noise representation, conditional-independence relation, and LIT candidate set while a simultaneous transformation of latent confounders, candidate target blocks, raw-utterance classes, denotation, and language encoder changes the true target and semantics but preserves all benchmark predictions and language-conditioned scores.
official_code_status: paper-specific official demo code verified at immutable commit; immutable R0 reproduction package not yet established
